job.title: Reception & Office Administrator
job.description:
Boutique Accounting Firm
Sydney CBD | Permanent Full-Time | Office Based

An exciting opportunity has become available for a Reception & Office Administrator to join a boutique accounting firm based in the Sydney CBD.
This is a varied role suited to someone who is reliable, proactive and highly organised, with previous experience working within an accounting or professional services environment. As the sole administrator within the firm, you will play an important role in keeping the office running smoothly while providing support to the management team and broader accounting team.

About the Role
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Welcoming and greeting clients in a professional and friendly manner
  • Managing incoming phone calls and enquiries
  • Coordinating incoming and outgoing mail
  • Maintaining the kitchen, filing areas and meeting rooms, including restocking and general organisation
  • Providing administrative support to the management team and broader accounting team
  • Preparing letters and correspondence
  • Maintaining and updating internal databases and records
  • Assisting with client on-boarding and related administration
  • Supporting the smooth day-to-day operation of the office
  • Assisting with ad hoc administrative tasks as required
About You
We are looking for someone who is:
  • Reliable, trustworthy and takes pride in their work
  • Highly organised with strong attention to detail
  • Proactive, with a genuine commitment to their role
  • Resilient and able to manage competing priorities
  • A confident communicator with strong interpersonal skills
  • Capable of using initiative and applying critical thinking
  • Comfortable working independently as the sole administrator
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word
  • Experienced working within an accounting firm or professional services environment
Experience with any of the following would be highly regarded:
  • ASIC processes, including annual statements and company incorporations
  • ABN and TFN registrations
  • Xero XPM
  • NowInfinity
  • FYI Document Manager
What's on Offer
  • Permanent, full-time position
  • Sydney CBD location, close to public transport
  • Work within a professional and supportive boutique accounting firm
  • A varied role with genuine responsibility and exposure across the business
  • Opportunity to become a key member of a close-knit team
If you're an experienced administrator who enjoys being the person who keeps everything organised and running smoothly please get in touch with Jessica Priebee jpriebee@quayappointments.com.au

job.title: Procurement Officer
job.description:
Procurement Officer
6-Month Contract | Likely to Extend | Procurement | Contracts | Stakeholder Engagement

We are currently seeking a Procurement Officer to join a busy procurement function within a well-established public sector organisation.
This is a 6-month contract initially, with a strong likelihood of extension longer term. The role will suit a procurement professional who understands the end-to-end procurement process and can confidently work with internal stakeholders and suppliers to deliver compliant, commercially sound outcomes.

The Role
Reporting to the Senior Procurement Business Partner, you will support a range of procurement activities from initial business requirements through to sourcing, tendering, contract award and ongoing contract management.
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Managing and reviewing end-to-end procurement and sourcing activities in line with established policies and procedures
  • Supporting the management of procurement panels and self-service purchasing channels
  • Assisting with contract management, including resolving issues and negotiating variations to purchase orders, contracts and agreements
  • Maintaining accurate procurement records and preparing reporting on procurement and contract activity
  • Providing procurement advice and support to internal stakeholders, including guidance on procurement processes, policy thresholds and best practice
  • Delivering training and support on procurement systems and processes
  • Identifying, managing and escalating procurement risks where required
  • Applying procurement governance and risk management frameworks across procurement activities
  • Supporting probity and governance requirements with internal stakeholders and suppliers
  • Keeping up to date with procurement policies, processes, legislation and relevant market developments
About You
We are looking for a procurement professional who can operate with a good level of autonomy and is comfortable working across multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
You will ideally have:
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications or equivalent professional experience, education and training
  • Experience across end-to-end procurement, including business planning, needs analysis, sourcing, tendering and contract award
  • Strong knowledge of procurement and contract management frameworks
  • The ability to manage procurement matters with minimal supervision
  • An understanding of procurement governance, risk and relevant legislative requirements
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Excellent stakeholder management and interpersonal skills
About the Opportunity
  • 6-month contract initially, with a strong likelihood of longer-term extension
  • Join a well-established public sector organisation
  • On-site parking available
  • Car travel is recommended, as the location is not close to public transport
  • Opportunity to work across a broad range of procurement, contracts, governance and stakeholder management activities
If you are a capable procurement professional who enjoys working closely with stakeholders and wants a role with broad exposure across the procurement lifecycle, please reach out to Jessica Priebee jpriebee@quayappointments.com.au with any additional questions.

job.title: Home Lending Specialist
job.description:
Home Lending Specialist 

Are you ready to take the next step in your lending career? We’re looking for a motivated lending professional who thrives on helping customers achieve their financial goals and wants to transition to a high-performing, phone-based lending environment.
Location: Newcastle
Salary: $100- $115K + super

Position Overview:
  • Engage with members over the phone to guide them through their lending options and help them achieve their goals.
  • Manage end-to-end loan applications, ensuring accuracy, compliance, and timely approvals.
  • Deliver an exceptional member experience while consistently driving conversion to loans.
  • Identify opportunities to cross-sell and match members with complementary products.
  • Maintain strong documentation and compliance standards.
What we’re looking for:
  • Branch or banking experience in home lending with a strong track record of success.
  • Cert IV in Finance and Mortgage Broking (or equivalent).
  • Minimum three years of end-to-end home lending experience, with a passion for helping customers achieve their goals.
  • Highly organised, motivated, and results-driven.
  • Skilled at identifying opportunities and converting them into outcomes.
Why this role:
  • Work for a Member Based Bank who's focus is on Customer outcomes and making a difference in their customer's lives.
  • Warm leads with focus on your ability to guide and convert through to settlement.
  • Guaranteed annual pay reviews in line with Enterprise agreement
  • One RDO each month
If you’re ready to step up, take ownership of your results, and make a real impact, we want to hear from you.
Please reach out to Jessica Priebee, jpriebee@quayappointments.com.au with any questions.

job.title: Business Development Executive
job.description:
Business Development Executive- Growth and Partnerships
Wheelers Hill | 12-Month Contract 
$85,000 + Super and Car Allowance| Convert to Permanent Employment
1 Month Completion bonus

Our client is a respected global organisation with operations across multiple markets. Their Australian team works closely with manufacturers and industrial customers, providing specialist products and solutions across a range of sectors. Joining a small and collaborative local team, this role offers significant autonomy, exposure to diverse markets and the opportunity to play a key role in driving business growth across Australia and New Zealand.

This is an excellent opportunity for a commercially minded professional with experience in the Industrial, Life Sciences, Healthcare, Chemicals or related industries to play a key role in growing the Australian business. Offering a blend of business development, account management and market analysis, you'll work closely with senior leadership to identify new opportunities, strengthen client relationships and contribute to long-term business growth.

About the Role
As Business Development Executive, you will be responsible for developing new business opportunities while managing and growing an existing portfolio of customers. You'll gain exposure to a diverse range of industries and work collaboratively to support strategic growth across the Australian market.
  • Proactively identify and engage with potential customers through market outreach, prospecting and relationship development.
  • Conduct market mapping and competitor research to identify industry trends, customer needs and new commercial opportunities.
  • Identify opportunities for new products, services and market segments within Australia.
  • Build an understanding of customer requirements and provide market intelligence to support business decisions.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with prospective customers, industry partners and key stakeholders.
  • Support the expansion of the organisation’s customer base and product offering.
  • Provide feedback and insights to management regarding market developments, competitor activity and growth opportunities.
  • Support sales planning, pricing strategies and broader business development initiatives.
  • Stay informed on relevant industry trends, regulations and market changes.
  • Support regulatory processes and licensing requirements to ensure compliance with Australian legislation.
  • Undertake domestic travel as required to meet with customers and industry stakeholders.
About You To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • A minimum of three years' experience in business development, sales or account management.
  • Experience within one or more of the following industries:
  • Wholesale or Industrial Trading
  • Industrial Products / Manufacturing
  • Chemicals
  • Mining & Resources
  • Healthcare
  • Life Sciences
  • A proactive and resilient approach with the ability to identify, develop and convert new business opportunities.
  • Strong relationship-building and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and presentation abilities.
  • Commercial acumen with the ability to analyse market trends and identify growth opportunities.
  • A willingness and ability to undertake domestic travel as required.
What's on Offer
  • Initial 12-month contract with genuine potential for permanent employment.
  • 1 month completion bonus.
  • Opportunity to join a respected international organisation with a strong global footprint.
  • A varied role combining business development, account management and strategic market analysis.
  • Exposure to diverse industries and the opportunity to contribute to the growth of the Australian business.
  • Wheelers Hill location with domestic travel opportunities.
If you're looking for a role where you can build strong client relationships, identify new opportunities and make a meaningful contribution to a growing business, we'd love to hear from you. For any questions please reach out to Jessica Priebee, jpriebee@quayappointments.com.au

job.title: Financial Accountant
job.description:
Financial Accountant
*Please note updated Duties to prior advertisement*
Well Respected Private School | Sydney's Inner West

An exciting opportunity has become available for an experienced Accountant to join the Business Office of a well respected independent school located in Sydney's Inner West.
Reporting to the Director of Finance you'll become part of a close-knit and collaborative finance team, playing a key role in delivering accurate financial reporting. 

Key Responsibilities
As the Financial Accountant, you will be responsible for:
  • Managing month-end and year-end financial reporting, including journals, reconciliations, accruals and prepayments.
  • Assisting with budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis and the preparation of quarterly budget reports for budget owners.
  • Preparing the annual payroll and staffing budget in collaboration with the Principal.
  • Supporting the external audit process, including preparing documentation, liaising with auditors and responding to audit queries.
  • Preparing FBT returns, workers compensation declarations and other statutory payroll reporting.
  • Supporting workforce reporting and providing payroll insights to assist College leadership with workforce planning and budgeting.
  • Driving continuous improvement, automation and best-practice controls across finance systems.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • CA or CPA qualification.
  • Minimum five years' experience in financial accounting.
  • Advanced financial reporting, reconciliation and technical accounting skills.
  • Excellent analytical skills with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Strong systems capability, with experience using finance systems.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities and build strong relationships across the business.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Experience within the education or not-for-profit sector will be highly regarded.
What's on Offer
  • Join one of Sydney's most respected independent schools.
  • Diverse and rewarding role across financial accounting, payroll and strategic workforce reporting.
  • Collaborative and supportive Finance team with close interaction across HR and College leadership.
  • Opportunity to contribute to strategic budgeting and workforce planning alongside senior leadership.
  • Beautiful Inner West location with convenient public transport access.
  • Stable, purpose-driven organisation with an outstanding workplace culture.
If you're looking for a role where you can utilise your financial accounting expertise while making a meaningful contribution to a highly regarded education provider, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply now or contact Jessica Priebee for a confidential discussion: jpriebee@quayappointments.com.au
